full_judgment:
MR. MD RUHUL AMIN, J:- Plaintiff-petitioner instituted Money Suit No. 192 of 1990 for realization of Tk. 11,94,024/- in the Court of Subordinate Judge Rangpur. The suit was decreed for Tk. 9,81,983.05 with interest. 

 4. The suit having been decreed on 23rd February, 1991 defendant-respondent preferred First Appeal No. 734 of 1991 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record upon arriving at the findings that the plaintiff Bank failed to explain why the balance quantity of pledge 2454 maunds 10 seers of tobacco leaves were not in the godown of the Bank and the Bank being in the possession and control of the godown it was the responsibility of the Bank to explain why the goods were not found in the Bank, that the loanee having defaulted in the payment of the loan money the bank ought to have sold the goods either by auction or by negotiation with the intending buyer but did not take any step for realization of the loan money upon selling the pledge goods which were in the godown of the Bank, that as the Bank failed to give explanation about the pledged 2454 maunds of tobacco leaves stored in its godown and that there being no evidence of selling the said tobacco leaves either by public auction or by private negotiation, the Suit filed by the Bank cannot be maintained and that the Bank having not explained as to absence of 2454 maunds and 10 seers of tobacco leaves from its godown and consequent thereupon Bank having failed to make out a case to have a decree in its favour, the trial court was in error in decreeing the Suit. The High Court Division dismissed the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree of the court of first instance. 

 5. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned counsel for the petitioner-Bank submits that defendant-respondent took loan of Tk. 7,00,000/- from the Bank and that he having had defaulted in the payment of the said amount, the High Court Division was in error in reversing the decree of the court of first instance on the finding that Bank failed to explain about the balance quantity of the pledged goods. He further submits that it was the duty of the defendant-respondent, the borrower to come forward to take delivery of the pledged goods and that to sell the same at his initiative and thereupon to adjust the loan amount on depositing the sale proceeds but the borrower having had not done so, the High Court Division erred in reversing the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge upon the view that if the pledged goods were sold either by public auction or private negotiation that would have fetched more amount than the amount due to the Bank and thereby the loanee would have got back the balance amount but the Bank did not do so. 

 6. It was the specific case of the defendant that he asked for delivery challan of 2454 maunds and odd of tobacco leaves but the Bank did not issue the delivery challan for taking out the pledge goods from the godown of the Bank. It was contended on behalf of the plaintiff that they published notice in the newspaper to sell the pledged tobacco leaves. But failed to explain what happened to the goods that were in the Bank's godown. It is not also denied by the Bank that 2454 maunds of goods were in the Bank's godown and that said goods were pledged with the Bank by the defendant. Since Bank could not explain what happened to the goods pledged with it, the Bank is not entitled to the decree sought in the suit. 

 7. In view of the discussions made herein above we find no reason to interfere with the judgment and decree dated 19''' July, I 999 of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 734 of 1991.
